searchText: thanks for reporting. Possibly this might be some glitch in evmone which "refilled" these tests. However, IIRC Besu passed similar tests when we were experimenting with this, so not sure. I'll look into this more closely next week. If you're curious whether apart from this these tests pass, you can ignore the gas limit change failures, they should be irrelevant to the gist of those tests. Don't you think this might be on the filling side which fills those blocks? I'll summon EEST here as well 🙂 <@892053833121923094> ? I will disable the gas limit check to see if we pass, if these are indeed refills we should pass them 🙂 First sanity check to check is whether you pass the "source" tests from `ethereum/tests` v14.1 release (`BlockchainTests/GeneralStateTests` IIRC). The main differences from those old ones are (should be): some bytecode is eof-wrapped and test is targetting Osaka. But I'd still suspect evmone refilling is the culprit, which I'll look into soon™️ Ahh wait I just realized that the t8ntool also reports the complete blocks (it should of course do so EEST can get relevant info like state root, block hash) so yeah maybe it's something on your side 🙂 Also a check for Besu maybe that in the blockchain test runner the gas limit check is not enforced? 🙂 I get additional errors also `Invalid block: base fee not correct block header number=1 ` Osaka EOFWrap bugs EthJS / Evmone
